rows.text: The fingerprint machinery and capability ladder and all other machinery are supposed to work in harmony with each other. There is no reason why any of this should no either work, work in the envisaged way, and work in harmony with everything else in the harness as a whole. The singe unifying goal of this project has been that of a science/STEM calculator, problem entered into the system and a definitive, reliable, repeatable answer out, just as is the case with any normal calculator. After all 4+4 will always equal 8. How can a system that gives a different answer every time be considered a serious or useful tool? LLM’s are a little different however. Answers can sometimes vary defending on their training data, how the question is formed, the skill of the researcher asking it, what area of their training data they might access on any given day (which doesn’t always appear to be the same), but providing this remains our direction of travel and any results produced by the system stands up to subsequent scrutiny and testing, this variability may be regarded as acceptable. Reproducibility in these conditions, may however ultimately become a separate step, either performed by the models, or the HIL, or both. I am undecided how this should work. We should probably ask the other models in a free panel review for their take on this. Reproducibility is after all a founding principle of the scientific method. We probably shouldn’t neglect it.

rows.text: No. We reset immune memory for the upcoming live experiments, since simulation can probably only tell us so much about how this facility will function in real live/paid experiments. There should be a facility for researchers to select a switch in the upcoming UX build if they want immune memory to persist between different experiments, or if they want it to be reset between experiments. For us in our upcoming use case, since our models won’t change (or perhaps at least not much, as we may add Kimi K3 back into the mix at some point), probably the best strategy is to leave the default in this case set to on, so that it can persist between experiments? Which brings up another issue we have discussed in the recent past, which is that overall, adding, removing, or changing models in the harness should be an entirely trivial affair (by design) and should not require major code changes to enable researchers to do so. The question is, is it? Have we adequately addressed this particular design objective?
rows.why: the immune memory was reset and the suite records the reset as the reason its 6 memory tests skip, re-arming as soon as a run writes a record
